newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka begins sending food to rebel areas.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka begins sending food to rebel areas.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Saturday began transporting much-needed food supplies to the northern, rebel-held Wanni region, where hundreds of people are said to have been displaced by the latest military offensive.

Aid workers in the north said that lorries were being loaded at Paraiyanalankulam, some 35 km (22 km) west of Vavuniya, and would be escorted into the Wanni region by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
"The lorries are being loaded and we will escort them," said an ICRC official in Colombo.
He said more lorries were expected to leave Paraiyanalankulam on Sunday.
The government agent for Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, said on Friday that 40 trucks would carry food to the Wanni on Sunday.
Kandiah Ganesh said food was short in some areas of the Wanni and immediate supplies were needed.

He said the Defence Ministry had approved a route through western Mannar town to northern Kilinochchi and northeastern Mullaitivu districts, where the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels are fighting government troops.

Aid workers have said that food stocks in the Wanni were strained by additional numbers joining the list of displaced and by government supplies grinding to a halt after the latest offensive, began earlier this month.
Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, have accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the pretext of opening a supply route.
They said earlier this week that the government had started a "food siege" and that the refugee crisis was spiralling out of control.
The rebels said in an overnight statement on Saturday that large-scale demonstrations have been held in the Wanni by people demanding immediate start to food convoys.

It said that Tamil civilians in the Wanni had to depend upon food from outside because the government has displaced huge numbers of them, destroyed their crop and closed all entry points for goods to enter the region.
The Defence Ministry said earlier this week that most of the Wanni except Kilinochchi district had sufficient food stocks for the next few weeks.
It said several thousand tonnes of wheat flour, rice, sugar and milk powder had been sent to the Wanni since October last year.
